claims.text: DonHangApp.build returns a MaterialApp with title 'Đơn Hàng', a theme, and home: ProductListScreen(apiClient: apiClient).

ProductListScreen is a StatefulWidget; the build of its State class _ProductListScreenState returns a Scaffold with an AppBar (title Text 'Đơn Hàng', a login IconButton), a FutureBuilder body (spinner while waiting, then a ListView.builder of ListTile with Text title and trailing), and a FloatingActionButton with a refresh Icon.
scripts/up.sh runs flutter build web, and the app-web container serves the build on http://localhost:8081.
In Flutter, UI is built from widgets, including layout (Padding, Center) and whole screens (Scaffold); widgets compose into a tree via build methods and child/children arguments.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: Introduction to widgets; Building user interfaces with Flutter

claims.text: Widgets are immutable descriptions; when something changes, build runs again and the framework diffs the new description against the previous one to find the minimal changes to apply to the underlying render tree.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: Introduction to widgets ('the framework diffs against the previous description')

claims.text: Widgets are lightweight, short-lived objects, so building a new widget description is cheap.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: Flutter architectural overview (widgets are cheap to create)

claims.text: Flutter's widget tree plays the role nested HTML elements play for a web page: containment level by level.
Flutter is a toolkit for building an app's UI in the Dart language; flutter build web produces files a browser can run.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: overview; flutter build web

claims.text: MaterialApp.title is the app's name as known to the platform (e.g. the browser tab title on the web), not the AppBar title text.
A FutureBuilder builds again when its future completes; snapshot.data then holds the future's result.
